title: Nighthawk OpsBridge — POC Account Brief (Agent Assist + Tool Calling)
executive_summary: Nighthawk builds a modular contact center orchestration layer used by ~150+ mid-market retailers. They want LLM-powered agent assist plus strict, idempotent tool-calls into their existing ticketing and refunds APIs. Their risk posture is conservative on refunds (0 tolerance for duplicates) and security-heavy (SAML, audit logs, KMS, EU data residency). POC is focused on (1) agent assist latency/quality on Hosted API, (2) tool-calling adapter through a customer-controlled gateway inside VPC, (3) spike simulation to validate fallback/backoff policies for 3rd-party rate limits.
traffic_profile: Normal ~10k msgs/day across customers; seasonal spikes 6–8x during flash sales (~120k msgs/day). Main concerns: tail latency + rate-limited downstream ticketing endpoints returning 429s.
latency_throughput_targets: Agent-assist suggestion latency target: p95 <275ms (original ask was <250ms; updated after reviewing transcript pre-processing overhead). End-to-end ticket creation workflow SLA target: <1.2s goal; accept async fallback during heavy spikes.
model_preferences: They want to test open models (LLaMA variants) and Redwood-verified models; quantized variants acceptable for cost. Must have deterministic tool-call payloads + schema enforcement (function/tool calling).
primary_ask: Reliable idempotent tool-calling for create/update ticket flows; automated refund authorization with an audit trail; rapid escalation path to human ops via API callouts.
integration_details: Customer uses an internal ticket system (OpsAPI v3) behind VPC with mutual TLS. Redwood calls a customer-hosted gateway function that enforces rate limits and translates payloads to OpsAPI v3 + refunds service. SE guidance remains: keep adapter thin; make idempotency keys first-class; treat 429/5xx as retriable with queue fallback.
poc_scope: 2-week POC (target window 2026-03-10 through 2026-03-24): (1) agent-assist latency baseline on Hosted API using sample transcripts, (2) tool-calling adapter to refunds microservice (idempotent endpoint), (3) spike simulation with synthetic load to validate fallback policies.
poc_success_criteria: Agent assist: p95 <275ms on target prompts after transcript normalization; Tool-calling: 99% correct idempotent ticket creations (no duplicates) + 0 duplicate refunds; Resilience: graceful fallback to async queue for <=5% of requests under peak with no user-visible failures.
key_quotes: “If the model triggers duplicate refunds that's a showstopper.” — Head of Ops
“Prefer private control plane for audit logs.” — VP Security
current_blockers: DPA redlines still pending final customer legal review (data residency language largely agreed, but retention + subprocessor notification timeline under discussion).
Customer SAML metadata exchange is completed in test, but production SAML configuration is waiting on their IdP change window (ETA early April).
Rate-limit behavior under real flash-sale traffic patterns still unvalidated (synthetic harness looks promising; need confirm with their historical distribution + burst profile).
security_notes: Must keep PII out of hosted logs for EU customers; require KMS encryption for any persisted KV cache; SSO (SAML) for admin console; SOC2 required before production go-live. Customer requested (a) explicit data retention policy language, (b) option to disable caching for EU tenants. Current proposed approach: keep caching configurable per tenant, default-off for EU in POC; document behavior in security addendum.
technical_risks: External ticketing/tier-2 endpoints can return 429s under spike. Customer preference: automatic backoff + queue-to-worker fallback; per-customer routing to alternative endpoints when available. Also observed occasional hallucinated ticket fields in early demo; mitigation is stricter JSON schema + field-level validation in gateway.
pricing_sensitivity: Mid-market; open to reserved capacity if cost predictability + SLOs are met. Interested in Optimize recommendations to reduce token costs for templated prompts. Internal note: Dedicated pools likely required for flash-sale consistency if they expand scope past POC.
recommended_package_direction: If POC passes: propose Dedicated for consistent latency + audit needs; Hosted API remains acceptable for non-peak but their flash-sale posture suggests dedicated capacity. Include an explicit async fallback workflow (create-ticket accepted + webhook completion) for peak bursts.

doc_body: Account brief owner notes (CS): Keep this doc ‘living’ through POC; convert into handoff notes if/when they buy.
Context
- Nighthawk = modular contact center orchestration layer for mid-market retailers.
- They’re integrating agent assist + tool calling into ticketing + refunds flows.
What they care about most
- Zero tolerance for duplicate refunds (explicitly called out as a showstopper).
- Deterministic tool-call payloads + schema enforcement + gateway-side validation.
- Handling spikes gracefully (flash sales) without blowing up downstream systems.
POC plan recap
- Agent assist latency + quality baseline on Hosted API.
- Tool-calling adapter to refunds service (idempotent endpoint) + ticket create/update via OpsAPI v3.
- Spike simulation + fallback path (async queue + accepted response).
Security/compliance
- EU: no PII in hosted logs; data residency requirements in DPA; prefer ability to disable caching for EU tenants.
- KMS encryption for any persisted KV cache; audit logging; SOC2 required pre-prod.
Where we are now
- Gateway + mTLS working in test.
- Demo surfaced occasional hallucinated ticket fields; fix is schema tightening + allowlist validation.
- Synthetic load improved; need validation against real burst distribution.
Handoff cues (if this turns into a deal)
- Dedicated likely needed for flash-sale season if they go beyond pilot.
- Keep a crisp ‘refund confirm’ UX requirement in any SOW; audit log must be mandatory.
- Document caching behavior per-tenant for EU; make default-off if legal remains sensitive.
